summary.text: A divergent boundary is a line between two tectonic plates that are moving away from each other.
Molten rock from below fills the gap the plates leave and becomes new crust, so rocks nearest the boundary are younger than rocks farther away on the same plate.
Most active ones are mid-ocean ridges between oceanic plates, while on land they start as rifts that become rift valleys such as East Africa's Great Rift Valley.

facts.label: Ocean examples
facts.value: Mid-Atlantic Ridge and East Pacific Rise

facts.label: Plate travel
facts.value: Many hundreds of kilometers over millions of years

facts.label: Magnetic signature
facts.value: Symmetrical reversal stripes on both sides of ridges

items.prompt: A geologist collects rock right at a mid-ocean ridge crest, then again far away on the same plate. How do their ages compare?

options.label: The ridge rock is older, as it formed first
The distant rock is older
Both are the same age
Age depends only on water depth

items.explain: New crust forms at the boundary and moves away, so rocks closest to the boundary are younger than rocks farther off.

items.prompt: Magnetic stripes on one side of a mid-ocean ridge match those on the other side like a mirror. Why?

options.label: Ship compasses drift the same way both ways
Ocean currents sort iron grains into bands
New crust spreads both ways as the poles flip
Volcanoes on each side erupt at random times

items.explain: New crust forms at the ridge center and moves off to both sides, and its banding tracks Earth's polar reversals, so each side carries the same pattern.

items.prompt: Two parts of a continent begin pulling apart from each other. What appears first along the line between them?

options.label: A deep ocean trench
A tall folded mountain chain
A curved chain of volcanic islands
A rift that can grow into a valley

items.explain: Divergent boundaries within continents first produce rifts, which eventually become rift valleys.

items.prompt: Two neighbouring stretches of a mid-ocean ridge open at different speeds. What forms between them?

options.label: Large faults where seafloor slides sideways
A new zone where one plate dives under
A single hotspot volcano
A gap where spreading simply stops

items.explain: Where adjacent ridge blocks spread at different rates, massive transform faults form, and these fracture zones are a major source of submarine earthquakes.

items.prompt: What mainly melts the rock beneath a spreading rift so that lava can pour out?

options.label: Water from a sinking slab of seafloor
Rising hot mantle and a drop in pressure
Friction from plates grinding past each other
Heat from ancient meteorite impacts

items.explain: Mantle material rises beneath the boundary, bringing heat and lowering pressure, which melts rock and forms large lava flows.

items.prompt: Old ridges far from a spreading center sit deeper in the ocean than the active ridge crest. What explains that?

options.label: Heavy sediment slowly crushed them down
Ocean currents wore their tops away
They were built lower from the start
They cooled, shrank and sank with age

items.explain: Older ridge crests are deeper because the rock has contracted as it cooled and subsided over time.
